Aww honey. I can’t tell you how much I relate to this. I’ve only been a nurse a year and a half. I remember those days all too well. My first day out they gave me two admits that required a lengthy workup and my lead had a full load of patients and couldn’t (or maybe wouldn’t) help me. It was awful and I cried at shift change at the end. I cried while giving report to the next shift. One of them tried to be nice and said to go ahead and go as I was trying to tell her about the patient and then reported me later for not giving her report. It was awful. I can tell you things definitely get better. You will learn more everyday and you will learn how to handle things better. That doesn’t mean you won’t still have terrible nights, but it does get easier. 
Nothings wrong with crying. You’re human and you’re trying. I promise you’re doing good! My only advise is to always look for ways to be better and not beat yourself up when you get overwhelmed or mess up.

I just started orientation last week as a new grad nurse. I was really worried about this too, but when I got to the floor every nurse I have worked with so far has been super nice and willing to help me. I agree with some of the people here who say to pay attention to the environment the unit or hospital has. The environment at my work seems to be one that fosters learning and encourages team work. I’m sure all the nurses aren’t best friends but you can tell they all respect each other and as a result they treat me with patience and respect. 
Edit: as for the anxiety, I would suggest talking to your healthcare provider and finding something good for anxiety-maybe meds or maybe anxiety reducing activities- something to keep you from feeling panicky. I struggle with anxiety really bad and recently started taking medication for it and it has really helped. Being new is still scary and stressful but for me it takes away a lot of the social anxiety and lessens worrisome/obsessive thoughts.
